title: catch-up 5: two-provider test that a follower recovers what it missed
description:
docs/design/mimi-catchup.md, the end-to-end proof, and the evidence for the working-group proposal.

Two providers on one in-process server as the existing tests do (crates/mimid-server/tests/jmap_two_providers.rs is the model): alice on the hub, bob on a follower. Take the follower off the air, have alice send and commit, bring the follower back, and require that bob sees every message in hub order with nothing missing and nothing duplicated.

Then the honest negative: push the gap outside the retention window and require that bob's user is TOLD, rather than shown a conversation with a hole.

Oracle: what alice's agent encrypted, compared with what bob's agent decrypts, independently of the catch-up code; and the hub's own sequence, compared with the order bob applied.

This bead is what makes the proposal in the parent credible: the chairs have been gated on implementation evidence since the 2026-01-13 chair message, so a WG issue arrives with running code or it does not arrive.
close_reason: Done in 33de78f9. Two real provider stacks, real HTTP, real hub sequence numbering, catchUp from the hub's published directory, and the follower's automatic fill: one test recovers what a hub gave up on, one has retention prune it first so the hub answers a real 410 and the follower moves the gone count instead. Oracle is outbox_capture, taken outside the catch-up code. NOT run against another implementation: still only mimid talking to mimid.
